findings.title: Task 4 changes shipModule.commands, but tests/ftlTargeting.test.ts pins the old list and no task updates it
findings.claim: Task 4 Step 3(c) appends 'pewFire' to shipModule.commands. tests/ftlTargeting.test.ts:169 asserts the exact old list, ['laserLock', 'torpLock', 'laserCharge', 'missileLaunch']. Task 4 neither edits that test nor runs it. Task 5 Step 6 then runs the `ftlTargeting` filter, which fails, and that failure is neither of the two kinds its triage allows: (a) a trajectory pin, or (b) another weapon's numbers moved by the Hunter's pew.
findings.evidence: plan L1234 (shipModule.commands gains 'pewFire'); plan L1292 (Task 4's test list has no ftlTargeting); plan L1552-1557 (Task 5's run includes ftlTargeting and its triage has only kinds (a) and (b)); tests/ftlTargeting.test.ts:L169 `expect(shipModule.commands).toEqual(['laserLock', 'torpLock', 'laserCharge', 'missileLaunch'])`
findings.why: Task 4 commits with a red test it never ran. The Task 5 subagent then hits a failure its instructions give no way to resolve.
findings.fix: In Task 4 Step 5, add (c): tests/ftlTargeting.test.ts line 169 becomes `expect(shipModule.commands).toEqual(['laserLock', 'torpLock', 'laserCharge', 'missileLaunch', 'pewFire']);   // W-1`. Add tests/ftlTargeting.test.ts to Task 4 Step 6's run and to Step 7's `git add`.

findings.title: Clicks on the console blocks reach the canvas, so clicking the Weapons panel or the new PEW row fires a round
findings.claim: Decision 8 says the cards and the contact window take their own pointer events. That is true only of the elements styled `pointerEvents: 'auto'`: Buttons, the card hit boxes, HelmStation's throttle box and the contact window. The Stage root is `pointerEvents: 'none'`, and that is inherited by the Panel backgrounds, every PixelText, the status table, the tab strip gaps, the side column and the new PEW row and pips (Task 9 adds no pointer capture to them). The pointer source listens on the canvas and records any button-0 press as a click. Task 8's pewClick only checks `onMap && station === 'weapons'`, so a press anywhere on the Weapons block that is not a button fires a pew toward the bottom-left, clamped into the cone. That includes clicking the PEW card itself. The Flight seat already filters these blocks for exactly this reason (flightPointer's BLOCKS).
findings.evidence: plan L35 (Decision 8's claim); plan L2207-2211 (pewClick has no over-a-block check); plan L2545-2550 (PEW row: Box/PixelText only); src/renderer/src/ui/stage/Stage.tsx:L7 (`pointerEvents: 'none'`); src/renderer/src/ui/duel/WeaponsStation.tsx:L52 and src/renderer/src/ui/stage/Button.tsx:L60 (only these are 'auto'); src/renderer/src/app/duel/duelMode.ts:L58 (pointer source on the canvas); src/renderer/src/app/duel/input.ts:L227 (any button-0 pointerdown becomes `click`); src/renderer/src/app/duel/flightPointer.ts:L9-23 (`inside`/BLOCKS filter for the Flight map)
findings.why: This is hit in ordinary play: a gunner who clicks the PEW card, its pips, or just misses the FIRE/LAUNCH buttons spends a third and fires a stray round. Every such round is also a crew shot that turns the holding Hunter hostile.
findings.fix: In Task 8 Step 5, add `&& overOpenWeaponsMap(click, shown)` to pewClick. Write that helper beside flightPointer's BLOCKS (or export a shared one) covering TABS, STATUS (its height from the readout rows), SIDE/SIDE_H, the Weapons STATION rect from stationTop('weapons') and, while shown, CONTACT. A click over a block falls through to today's contact.click path. Add a pewInput or contactScene test: a click at weaponCard('laser').y - 10 (on the PEW row) queues no pew.

findings.title: Moving a Task 6 tuning knob breaks constants pinned in tests/pewHunter.test.ts, and Task 6 never updates that file
findings.claim: Task 6 Step 4 may change HUNTER_PEW_ERROR (4 → 6 → 8), HUNTER_PEW_GAP (12 → 20) and HUNTER_PD_CHANCE (0.5 → 0.3/0.8). Task 5's test pins the derived values: HUNTER_PEW_ERROR_STEPS 728, HUNTER_PD_ODDS 120 and HUNTER_PEW_GAP 12. Its pinned PD_SEED and the 0.02..0.6 rate band also depend on those knobs. Task 6 Step 6 runs tests/pewHunter.test.ts and expects PASS, but has no step to re-pin it, and the file is not in Task 6's `git add`.
findings.evidence: plan L1361 (`toBe(728)`, `toBe(120)`, `toBe(12)`); plan L1357, L1409 (PD_SEED pinned from the console line); plan L1663-1666 (the knobs Task 6 may move); plan L1740 (pewHunter.test.ts in Task 6's PASS run); plan L1749 (git add lacks tests/pewHunter.test.ts)
findings.why: In every tuning branch that moves a knob, Task 6's own verification cannot pass as written, and the subagent has no rule for what to change.
findings.fix: Make the first assertion derive from the knobs: `expect(HUNTER_PEW_ERROR_STEPS).toBe(Math.floor((HUNTER_PEW_ERROR / 360) * AIM_STEPS)); expect(HUNTER_PD_ODDS).toBe(Math.round(1 / (HUNTER_PD_CHANCE * DT)));` and drop the literal HUNTER_PEW_GAP pin. Alternatively, add a Task 6 Step 6 bullet: 'if any knob moved, update tests/pewHunter.test.ts's pinned numbers and re-pin PD_SEED from its printed line (Task 5 Step 5's rule)', and add the file to Step 7's git add.

findings.title: Task 5's 'The imports become' block drops hunter.ts's existing ./science and ./weapons imports
findings.claim: hunter.ts imports `enemyHostile` from './science' and `canLaunch, laserEligible, laserFull, type ShipInput` from './weapons', on lines 14-15, after the tuning import. Task 5 Step 4(a) gives the complete new import block and neither line is in it. A subagent that replaces the import block verbatim removes them, and tsc fails on enemyHostile, canLaunch, laserEligible, laserFull and ShipInput.
findings.evidence: plan L1458-1471 (the replacement import block ends at the tuning import); src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/hunter.ts:L14-15 (the two imports it omits)
findings.why: The plan is executed verbatim, and as written this step does not compile.
findings.fix: Append the two lines to the block in plan L1460-1471: `import { enemyHostile } from './science';` and `import { canLaunch, laserEligible, laserFull, type ShipInput } from './weapons';`. Or reword (a) as 'replace lines 5-13 (through the tuning import); lines 14-15 stay'.

findings.title: Task 9's duelSounds insertion only compiles if placed before gunHit's closing brace, and the step does not say so
findings.claim: The inserted text starts with `} else if (e.kind === 'pewFire') {` and ends without a closing brace, so it relies on gunHit's existing `}` on duelSounds.ts:37 to close pewHit. The step says to insert it 'after the gunHit branch (before `if (hitsCrew(e))`)'. Read literally, that is after line 37's `}`, which gives `}\n} else if`, a syntax error.
findings.why: Two implementers would place this differently, and one placement does not parse.
findings.fix: Give the replacement whole: lines 34-37 (`} else if (e.kind === 'gunHit') { ... }`) become the gunHit branch followed by the pewFire and pewHit branches, ending in `}`. Or say 'insert between line 36 and the `}` on line 37'.

findings.title: Task 6's tuning ladder has no stop rule for the Hound, misstates which knobs act on the Valkyrn, and re-pins only five named tests
findings.claim: (1) After knob 5, a Hound that still fails has no instruction; only the Valkyrn branch says 'stop and report'. (2) Item 6 says HUNTER_PEW_ERROR is 'the only knob both share'. But HUNTER_PEW_GAP and HUNTER_PD_CHANCE also act on the Valkyrn duel: the Hunter's attack and point defence run against any crew class, including the Valkyrn's torpedo. (3) Step 6 re-pins only the five named files. A different trajectory pin that Task 5 Step 6 lists as kind (a) (it asks for 'the kind (a) list' in the commit body) has no re-pin step anywhere. (4) There is no fallback if no seed 1..10 sends exactly the six kinds that duelScripted needs.
findings.evidence: plan L1662-1667; plan L1554, L1557, L1564 (Task 5's kind (a) list); plan L1731-1736 (only five files re-pinned); src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/hunter.ts:L84-121 (hunterThink is class-agnostic, so the Hunter's pew fires at the Valkyrn)
findings.why: The brief requires concrete knobs and a concrete stop rule. As written, a failing Hound gate, or an unlisted pinned test, leaves the subagent guessing.
findings.fix: Add: 'if the Hound still fails after knob 5, stop and report the recorded lines'. Correct item 6 to name every knob that acts on the Valkyrn (HUNTER_PEW_ERROR, HUNTER_PEW_GAP, HUNTER_PD_CHANCE). Add to Step 6: 're-pin every kind (a) test listed in Task 5's commit body by the same rule (keep the assertion, update the value, add the history note)'. For duelScripted: 'if no seed qualifies, assert that the kinds include pewFire and stop and report'.

findings.title: Task 10's `npm run test:determinism` never runs a duel, so it does not prove the pew deterministic across runtimes
findings.claim: The determinism harness replays only the sector fixture (variants hound-2 and hound-3); nothing under scripts/determinism mentions the duel. The new pew math (dirBetween's sqrt, segmentEntry, interceptTime, the Hunter's rng draws) therefore gets no Node/Electron/Firefox comparison. Task 10 Step 3 and the self-review present this run as the spec's cross-runtime check.
findings.evidence: plan L2649-2652, L2691 ('Determinism on Node, Electron, Firefox (Task 10)'); tests/determinismHarness.test.ts:L44-45 (variants hound-2/hound-3 only); Grep 'duel|Duel' in scripts/determinism/ finds no files; spec L128
findings.why: The brief requires bit-determinism across the three runtimes, and the plan reports it as verified when the step cannot fail on a pew desync.
findings.fix: Either state in Task 10 that test:determinism covers only the sector, so the duel's cross-runtime guarantee rests on the guard rules (only + − × ÷ and sqrt), and report it as not verified. Or add a step that runs the scripted duel golden (runDuel at DUEL_GOLDEN_SEED) in the Electron and Firefox pages and compares its hashes with Node's.

findings.title: The Weapons help text and sit card never mention the left-click pew
findings.claim: Task 8 adds the Settings row, but the in-game help for the Weapons seat stays '1/2 PICK WEAPON, CLICK ROOM', and the sit card still reads 'WEAPONS: CLICK A WEAPON, THEN A ROOM'. The primary weapon is then discoverable only from the PEW row's 'L-CLICK MAP' hint.
findings.why: A new primary weapon whose control is listed only in Settings and in a small hint is easy to miss in the owner's playtest.
findings.fix: Add 'L-CLICK MAP PEW' to the weapons help list and the sit card's keys in Task 8 or Task 9, and update their tests.
